subject: End-of-quarter assessment vignettes, retro asks, closure plan
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Draft assessment vignettes + quick asks before QBR prep

Team —

Attached is the working set of Q2 assessment vignettes and my first-pass annotations (Q2-assessment-vignettes.pdf). I pulled together 12 short customer vignettes that surface the most contested scoring points across product, infra, and go-to-market. The goal is to: 1) surface evidence we used for each score, 2) capture a one-paragraph rationale, and 3) highlight any unresolved tension we should flag in the QBR.

Asks:
- Laura: can you sanity-check the product evidence bullets by EOD Tue? Focus on the 3 vignettes marked RED (pages 4, 8, 11).
- Vivek: if you have any top-line guidance on grading trade-offs (risk tolerance vs. conservatism) please share — I want to avoid last-minute re-rates.
- Marissa/Ben: I need a one-paragraph customer-facing narrative for the two major escalations (Nimble + Acme) so we can include a short communications appendix.

Notes: I annotated potential alternative scores where the evidence is ambiguous — see column B in the attached score-annotations.xlsx. For transparency, I plan to include the short evidence snippets in the appendix we share with leadership.

I plan to bake your edits into a closure draft and send to Nimble (Sarah) and Acme contracts for factual review before the QBR.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Product Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft assessment vignettes + quick asks before QBR prep

Irene — thanks for pulling this together, very helpful. Quick pass attached as inline notes (I added a handful of evidence links and reordered the product-led vignettes so the narrative flows).

Top-level from my side:
- The RED vignettes: agree they're borderline. For vignette #4 (latency regression), the telemetry evidence supports a conservative downgrade for the quarter, but we should call out the confounder (A/B rollout overlap) in the notes so the comms team doesn't overstate.
- For the embedding quality vignette (#8), I recommend we add the eval anchor (eval-run-20270422.json) to the appendix; that should reduce the perceived subjectivity.

I added one proposed phrasing for the Nimble narrative — short, factual, and offers a next-step (technical deep-dive next week).

On the grading trade-offs: I favor consistency (less re-rating across quarters) unless there's a clear demonstrable regression. That should make our QBR stories easier to compare.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product Management | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft assessment vignettes + quick asks before QBR prep

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of evidence-first pack I want in front of the execs. A couple of short decisions from me: 

1) Scoring posture: maintain consistency across quarters unless the evidence is strong (i.e., >2 independent signals). For the RED latency vignette, leave the score as-is but call out the confounder prominently in the executive slide so we don't misattribute.

2) Communication approach: for Nimble, use Laura's phrasing but add a clear remediation timeline (technical deep-dive by May 12; follow-up score re-check during week of May 24). For Acme, keep the narrative factual and offer a post-QBR operational sync — avoid public-facing language that reads like an apology.

3) Closure plan: Irene/Marissa — please produce a short slip (2 slides) for the QBR that contains (a) evidence summary, (b) proposed final score, (c) comms snippet, and (d) next-step. Receiver for the slides: me and the CEO. I want them in my inbox by EOD Thu.

Irene/Marissa, if you need me to sign off on any alternative wording before send, loop me in.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Operating Officer | Redwood Inference
